help.subtitle: What this template does, who built it and which version you are running
help.aboutSubtitle: A from-scratch admin template, not a template fork
help.aboutBody: Tableau Embed Hub is an open-source admin console for embedding Tableau Cloud and Tableau Server analytics. Built from scratch on shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS v4 + Radix UI + TanStack Router, with no backend and no vendor fork: what you see is the whole source. It ships the scaffolding a multi-team dashboard needs — team-scoped URLs, page-level permissions, system configuration — plus a few real data pages instead of placeholder screens.

help.thirdPartyIntro: This project's own code is MIT-licensed. The build also ships the third-party components listed below; each stays under its own licence and copyright, and those terms apply to you as well. The full text lives in THIRD-PARTY.md in the repository, and 'pnpm licenses list' prints the complete list including transitive dependencies.

teams.title: Multi-team workspace
teams.body: Users sit above teams and can hold a different role in each. Every workspace URL carries its team slug (/t/{slug}/…), so a shared link keeps its context and two tabs can sit in two teams.

permissions.title: Page-level permissions
permissions.body: One route catalog drives the sidebar, the route guard and the roles × pages matrix on /permissions. Pages added later stay admin-only until granted (fail-closed).

tableau.title: Tableau embedding
tableau.body: Workbooks, views, favourites and recents, embedded with a Connected App JWT signed in the browser.

config.title: System configuration
config.body: The Config section holds deployment-wide settings, starting with SMTP: provider presets, live preflight checks and a password that is never written to disk.

profile.title: Your own profile
profile.body: Reached from the user menu at the bottom left — display name and email bound to the signed-in account, with role and teams shown read-only.

i18n.title: Internationalisation and theming
i18n.body: i18next dictionaries (en-US today, more locales later) plus light / dark / system themes, both switchable from the header.

quality.title: Behaviour locked by scripts
quality.body: Type checking plus Chrome-driven check suites (routes, permissions, SMTP, flow layout, i18n parity): the behaviours a type system cannot prove are asserted in a real browser.

Real access control belongs on a server: verify permissions per request, keep secrets server-side, and validate the sending domain (SPF / DKIM) before email goes live.

smtp.presetHint: Pick a provider to fill in host, port and encryption. Credentials are yours to enter.

smtp.hostHint: Host name only — no scheme, no path

smtp.passwordHint: Held in memory only — see the note below

check.hostHasScheme: Enter the host name only — drop the scheme (http://) and any path
check.hostChars: Host may only contain letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores
check.hostIntranet: “{{host}}” has no domain suffix — fine for an intranet relay, and it must still resolve in DNS
check.portRange: Port must be an integer between 1 and 65535
check.portWantsSsl: Port {{port}} is the implicit-TLS port: switch encryption to {{mode}}
check.portWantsStarttls: Port {{port}} normally pairs with STARTTLS, not SSL/TLS — connecting straight to TLS rarely works here
check.port25Blocked: Port 25 is commonly blocked outbound by ISPs and cloud providers — use 587 with STARTTLS
check.encryptionNone: Traffic is not encrypted — only acceptable on a trusted intranet relay
check.usernameMissing: No username: most providers reject unauthenticated mail. Leave it empty only for a trusted relay.
check.passwordMissing: No password or authorization code yet — sending will fail until you enter one
check.passwordWithoutUsername: A password is held, but there is no username to authenticate with
check.passwordNotNeeded: No credential needed for an anonymous relay
check.fromInvalid: From address is not a valid email address
check.providerCustom: Custom host — nothing to compare against a provider reference
check.providerMismatch: {{provider}} normally uses port {{port}} with {{mode}} — check the values above

smtp.localCheckNoteTitle: This check runs in the browser
smtp.localCheckNote: The template ships without a backend and a browser cannot open an SMTP socket, so the checks above cover the configuration itself: format, port/encryption consistency and provider reference values. The real handshake (EHLO → STARTTLS → AUTH) has to run server-side — wire the button to your API once it exists:
smtp.secretNote: The password is kept in memory for this session only and is never written to localStorage: a browser-side “encrypted” secret would ship its own key inside the bundle, so anyone who can read the bundle can decrypt it. Store it on the server instead (encrypted, never returned by the API) as soon as the backend lands.

components.subtitle: Every shared building block: page shell, theme tokens, project composites and UI primitives
components.introBody: Look here before hand-rolling a button, a filter bar or a dialog. Every entry lists its import path, a one-line purpose and a live preview.
components.introNote: A shared component belongs in src/config/component-catalog.ts (one entry) plus a demo in src/features/components/*-sections.tsx. Page skeleton rules live in docs/ui-conventions.md.
components.noPreview: No live preview — this one needs real page data. Open the page that uses it (see the description) or read its source.

section.layoutHint: Page skeleton and the containers that give every page the same rhythm.
section.actionsHint: Buttons and menus — route them through these so position and hierarchy stay consistent everywhere.
section.formsHint: Label, hint, error text, aria wiring and the readable width cap are all handled by FormField — do not hand-roll them.
section.dataHint: Tables, badges, summaries and loading placeholders.
section.filtersHint: One controlled filter bar plus useListFilters, shared by every list page.
section.overlaysHint: Dialogs, sheets, popovers, tooltips and the command palette.
section.feedbackHint: Notes, toasts, fallback pages and environment status.
section.hooksHint: State helpers that pair with the composites above.

shell.title: App shell
shell.hint: The frame around every page: sidebar, header and content padding. Numbers that exist as constants are imported from the source, so this table cannot drift.
shell.mockTitle: Sidebar anatomy — rendered with the real sidebar pieces
shell.noteTitle: Sidebar and mobile drawer share one width
shell.note: Both use the same constant ({{width}}). A second, larger mobile width is exactly what made the narrow-window drawer wider than the desktop sidebar — do not add one back.

tokens.title: Theme tokens
tokens.hint: Colors and radii are CSS variables in src/index.css. Use the token class (bg-card, text-muted-foreground) instead of a raw color — that is what makes dark mode work.

desc.pageContainer: Root wrapper for every page: the vertical rhythm (gap-6) and the single place where page width is decided — it fills the content area, no max-w.
desc.card: The standard container: header / content / footer sharing one inner spacing variable.
desc.tabs: Switch between sibling views inside one card without changing the route.
desc.collapsible: Show or hide a detail block in place.
desc.button: All six variants plus the sizes actually used in the app (default, sm, lg, icon).
desc.actionBar: The cancel + primary action pair: primary always right-most, stacked on narrow screens. Used by every dialog and form footer.
desc.dropdownMenu: Row actions and overflow menus, with labels, checkbox items, submenus and shortcuts.
desc.toggle: Two-state button (pressed / not pressed) for formatting-style controls.
desc.formField: A whole field in one component: label, control, hint or error, aria wiring and the readable width cap.
desc.label: Field label, wired to htmlFor by FormField.
desc.input: Single-line text input, including the invalid state.
desc.inputGroup: Input with addons (icon, prefix text, inline button) — the search box is built on it.
desc.select: Radix select. It renders no DOM of its own, so pass an explicit id when used inside FormField.
desc.checkbox: Boolean or multi-select checkbox with label.
desc.switch: On/off switch for settings that apply immediately.
desc.table: Data table. Long text columns must opt out of the default whitespace-nowrap, otherwise the page grows a horizontal scrollbar.
desc.badge: Short status or role marker; for tag-like data prefer a badge flow over a table.
desc.avatar: Avatar with fallback initials, plus grouped avatars for member previews.
desc.descriptionList: Label + value summary (about pages, detail panels), capped at 768px so values stay scannable.
desc.skeleton: Loading placeholder that matches the final layout.
desc.breadcrumb: Hierarchy trail. The app header shows the page title instead, so use this inside detail views.
desc.filterBar: Search + select + result count + reset as one controlled row. Filter state lives in the page (useListFilters).
desc.dialog: Modal for focused tasks; the footer uses ActionButtons.
desc.sheet: Side panel for secondary flows — the mobile sidebar is a Sheet too.
desc.popover: Anchored floating panel for small forms or pickers.
desc.tooltip: Explains icon-only controls. The provider is already mounted in main.tsx.
desc.command: Searchable command list (cmdk); also available as CommandDialog.
desc.noteCallout: Info / warning block for explanations and edge-case notes.
desc.toast: Transient feedback via sonner. <Toaster /> is mounted once in main.tsx.
desc.guardCard: Shared shell for forbidden, missing and empty states.
desc.configStatusCard: Environment check card: which Tableau site and AI provider are actually in effect.
desc.thumbnailCard: Workbook / view card with thumbnail, badges and a row menu. It needs real list data, so there is no preview here.
desc.listState: Loading / error / empty shell for a list inside a card. The third empty state (filtered to zero) stays in the page — its copy and its reset action are page-specific.
desc.useListFilters: Holds filter values, computes activeCount and resets to the module-level defaults. Pairs with FilterBar.
desc.useFormTouch: Decides when validation is shown: after a field is blurred, or after the primary action is pressed.

tableauUsers.subtitle: Users on the connected Tableau Cloud site, read from the REST API — site roles are written back through the same API
tableauUsers.boundaryBody: This table mirrors the connected Tableau site, not the demo accounts on /users. Nothing is copied into the browser: every sync is a fresh REST read, and a role change goes straight to Tableau. This build signs the JWT in the browser, so anyone who can open the page holds the site credentials — page permissions control visibility, not authorization.

error.noSeat: Tableau refused the change: no licence seat of that type is available on this site (409014).

error.invalidRole: Tableau rejected that site role as invalid for its version (400013).

error.unauthorized: Not authorized. The signed-in Tableau user is not a site administrator, or the JWT scope is missing (401002).
error.unknown: Tableau rejected the change. Check the site's users and licence seats, then try again.
